Source.Author: Shawn Brink
Source.SupportedClaim: The tutorial describes a Windows 10/11 all-user file context-menu submenu which requires administrator approval to add or remove and appears under Show more options in Windows 11.

Findings: The retained commands echo the shell-substituted path into PowerShell and reconstruct it by stripping presumed quote characters. The upstream thread documents a double-space issue in an earlier command form; the author updated the tutorial. A suggested alternative was then reported to fail with apostrophes. The current retained command's behavior for unusual paths has not been tested through Explorer.
Each supplied command ends with Start-Sleep 3600, keeping its console alive for one hour.

The attachment lists MD5, SHA1, SHA256, SHA384, SHA512, MACTripleDES and RIPEMD160. The supplied command invokes powershell, which selects Windows PowerShell 5.1 on the tested Windows host; its Get-FileHash accepts all seven listed algorithms. PowerShell 7.6.5 accepts only MD5, SHA1, SHA256, SHA384 and SHA512 and rejects MACTripleDES and RIPEMD160 at parameter validation.

A local synthetic file with double spaces, ampersand, percent sign, Unicode and an apostrophe was read via Get-FileHash -LiteralPath in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7.6.5. This tests cmdlet path handling only; it does not prove Explorer command-line substitution or registry integration.
The attached Show all command was not executed; no user file was opened.

LocalProbe.CommandRuntime: The supplied commands invoke powershell, not pwsh; local Windows PowerShell 5.1 is the relevant default runtime.

ImplementationImplications: A RIDE adaptation must pass the selected file path as an argument to an owned helper instead of reconstructing the path from echoed text.
Do not silently omit MACTripleDES or RIPEMD160; establish supported, maintained implementations or revise the requested submenu scope explicitly.
Replace the one-hour sleep with a reviewed output interaction.
Use per-user registry scope for the RIDE setting and verify saved-state restore and Windows 11 classic/Show more options behavior in a disposable guest.

Resolved: Current upstream tutorial menu placement and scope claims
Get-FileHash algorithm availability on the local Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7.6.5 installations
Partial: Upstream command/path failure evidence and safer adaptation requirements
Deferred: Owned helper deployment and command quoting across actual Explorer invocation
A supported implementation for every requested algorithm
Repeat apply, remove, exact saved-state restore, GUI and Windows 11 VM acceptance

Estimates.ReasonUnchanged: This is an additional v3 setting request; static source review and a synthetic cmdlet probe do not complete it or close a legacy migration outcome.
